questions.topic: Dataform: SQL Pipelines with Dependency Graphs
questions.question: What workload is Dataform primarily designed to manage?
options: Extraction of records from operational sources into a landing zone in object storage
Visual assembly of connector-based integration flows from prebuilt plugins
SQL transformations in BigQuery, built as a tested, version-controlled graph
Long-running streaming services that hold per-key state between invocations

questions.topic: Dataform: SQL Pipelines with Dependency Graphs
questions.question: What does a Dataform dependency graph determine?
options: The order in which actions run, letting independent branches proceed in parallel
The BigQuery reservation each compiled action draws its slots from at runtime
The Git branch a workspace's compilation result is published to on release
The physical partitioning each output table receives when it is created

questions.topic: Dataform: SQL Pipelines with Dependency Graphs
questions.question: Why use the Dataform ref function for an upstream table?
options: It rewrites the upstream model as a view so the reference resolves at run time
It caches the upstream result so the downstream model does not rescan the table
It grants the workflow's service account read access on the referenced dataset
It resolves the qualified relation name and declares the dependency at once

questions.topic: Dataform: SQL Pipelines with Dependency Graphs
questions.question: Which issue is found during compilation rather than BigQuery execution?
options: A service account that lacks permission to run the job on the dataset
A circular dependency between two of the project's declared actions
A source table whose column holds unexpected nulls the model mishandles
A query that exceeds a runtime resource limit during its final stage

questions.topic: Dataform: SQL Pipelines with Dependency Graphs
questions.question: An incremental model misses late events. What is the most appropriate design improvement?
options: Widen the predicate into a rolling lookback window and merge on a stable unique key
Add an assertion that the row count rises on every run, so gaps get flagged
Partition the target by ingestion time so the incremental filter prunes correctly
Declare an explicit dependency on the source so the model waits for it to land

questions.topic: Dataform: SQL Pipelines with Dependency Graphs
questions.question: How should a team isolate developer outputs while retaining one Dataform codebase?
options: Give each developer a Git branch and let releases pick the branch to compile
Have each developer hand-edit the model names in SQLX before they run them
Set workspace compilation overrides for the project, schema, or object prefix
Point each developer at a release configuration that pins production settings

questions.topic: Cloud Data Fusion at Awareness Level
questions.question: What is Cloud Data Fusion?
options: A managed Spark cluster service that runs submitted jobs on ephemeral nodes
A managed data integration service with a visual pipeline design environment
A managed Airflow environment for authoring Python DAGs of operator tasks
A managed SQL transformation tool that compiles a dependency graph for BigQuery

questions.topic: Cloud Data Fusion at Awareness Level
questions.question: What does a node in a Cloud Data Fusion pipeline commonly represent?
options: An IAM binding that grants the pipeline's identity access to one connector
A namespace that partitions applications and metadata inside the instance
A compute profile that fixes where and with what resources the run happens
A source, transform, sink, or action stage that records flow through

questions.topic: Cloud Data Fusion at Awareness Level
questions.question: What is the purpose of a Cloud Data Fusion compute profile?
options: It stores the pipeline's schema so downstream sinks can validate incoming records
It replaces the logical flow with an equivalent Beam pipeline before execution
It specifies where a pipeline runs and with what execution resources it runs
It holds the connection credentials each source plugin uses at run time

questions.topic: Cloud Data Fusion at Awareness Level
questions.question: When is Cloud Data Fusion a particularly suitable option?
options: When a team wants visual pipeline design plus a broad library of ready-made connectors
When the transformation is pure BigQuery SQL that should stay version-controlled
When a pipeline needs custom stateful streaming logic written in Beam code
When the requirement is log-based capture of a database's committed changes

questions.topic: Cloud Data Fusion at Awareness Level
questions.question: A pipeline succeeds in preview but fails at production volume. What is the best explanation?
options: Preview runs the same rows as production, so the difference must be a plugin bug
Preview bypasses the compute profile, so production used a different Spark version
Preview validates IAM only, so the design itself was never actually exercised
Preview uses a data subset, so scale, permissions, and edge cases stay untested

questions.topic: Cloud Data Fusion at Awareness Level
questions.question: A team needs deeply customized stateful streaming logic in code. Which alternative deserves strongest consideration?
options: Datastream, since it captures committed changes and lands them continuously
Dataflow, since Apache Beam expresses windowed state and custom transforms
Dataform, since incremental tables can hold state between scheduled workflow runs
Workflows, since parallel branches and retries can express a streaming loop

questions.topic: Composer vs Workflows: Choosing the Orchestrator
questions.question: Managed Service for Apache Airflow is based on which open source project?
options: Apache Airflow
Apache Cassandra
Apache Kafka
Apache Spark

questions.topic: Composer vs Workflows: Choosing the Orchestrator
questions.question: What does Google Cloud Workflows primarily coordinate?
options: Python DAGs of operator tasks running on a managed scheduler environment
Distributed record processing across a pool of autoscaled worker machines
Sequences of Google Cloud API and HTTP calls, with branching and retries
Visual pipelines of connector plugins executed on an ephemeral Spark cluster

questions.topic: Composer vs Workflows: Choosing the Orchestrator
questions.question: Which requirement most strongly favors Managed Airflow?
options: A single event that triggers three managed API calls and then a notification
Hundreds of scheduled DAGs needing backfills, sensors, and provider operators
A control flow that must run with no persistent orchestration environment
A transformation that should process its terabytes inside the orchestrator

questions.topic: Composer vs Workflows: Choosing the Orchestrator
questions.question: Which workload most strongly favors Workflows?
options: A portfolio of nightly DAGs with historical reruns and cross-DAG conventions
A pipeline whose logic is a custom Beam transform holding per-key state
A nightly job whose hundreds of task dependencies need Airflow's trigger rules
An event-driven chain of managed API calls needing no persistent scheduler

questions.topic: Composer vs Workflows: Choosing the Orchestrator
questions.question: Why should an orchestrated task accept a stable operation ID?
options: So the orchestrator can run every dependent branch of the DAG in parallel
So the runtime identity inherits the permissions the downstream service needs
So a retry after an unrecorded success can detect it instead of repeating it
So large payloads can be passed by reference rather than held as variables

questions.topic: Composer vs Workflows: Choosing the Orchestrator
questions.question: Where should a large BigQuery transformation normally execute?
options: In BigQuery or Dataform, with the orchestrator only starting and watching it
Inside the orchestrator's own variables, so each step can inspect the rows
Inside the DAG parser, so the schedule reflects the transformation's real cost
Inside the retry handler, so a failure re-runs the transformation immediately
